pages.name: Home
pages.purpose: Opening screen. Two big choices: Send files or Receive files.
pages.notes: Portrait. Paint everything you want on screen, including the app name and the words on the two buttons. Mark the two buttons as tap areas.

assets.name: home.png
assets.description: The full Home screen, finished, with both buttons in place.

regions.label: send_button
regions.action: tap to choose files and start sending

regions.label: receive_button
regions.action: tap to start receiving

pages.name: Sending
pages.purpose: Shown while this phone is sharing files. A QR code for the other phone to scan, and a list of what has been sent.
pages.notes: Leave the QR area as a plain white square (at least 640 px wide) and the list area empty. The app draws the QR code, the link text and the list of files into those areas. Paint the Stop button with its words.

assets.name: sending.png
assets.description: The full Sending screen with the QR square, list area and Stop button in place, but no QR code, link text or file names.

regions.label: qr_square
regions.action: the app draws the QR code here (keep it plain white)

regions.label: link_area
regions.action: the app writes the web link here

regions.label: file_list
regions.action: the app lists the files being sent and their progress here

regions.label: stop_button
regions.action: tap to stop sharing

pages.name: Receiving
pages.purpose: Shown while this phone is waiting for files. A QR code for the sender to scan, and a list of what has arrived.
pages.notes: Same idea as Sending but give it its own look so the two are easy to tell apart. Plain white QR square (at least 640 px), empty list area, Stop button with its words.

assets.name: receiving.png
assets.description: The full Receiving screen with the QR square, list area and Stop button in place, but no QR code, link text or file names.

regions.label: qr_square
regions.action: the app draws the QR code here (keep it plain white)

regions.label: link_area
regions.action: the app writes the web link here

regions.label: file_list
regions.action: the app lists the files received here

regions.label: stop_button
regions.action: tap to stop receiving

pages.name: Allow device
pages.purpose: A pop-up asking the host to approve a new phone or browser before it can transfer anything.
pages.notes: Just the pop-up box on a transparent background (it floats over the other screens). Leave space for a short message that the app writes. Paint the Allow and Deny buttons with their words.

assets.name: allow_popup.png
assets.description: The pop-up box with Allow and Deny buttons, transparent around it, no message text.

regions.label: message_area
regions.action: the app writes who is asking to connect here

regions.label: allow_button
regions.action: tap to let this device connect

regions.label: deny_button
regions.action: tap to refuse

pages.name: Choose how to share
pages.purpose: A pop-up shown after tapping Send or Receive: share on the same Wi-Fi or hotspot, or from anywhere (beta).
pages.notes: Just the pop-up box on a transparent background, like the Allow pop-up. Paint the words on the two big buttons. Leave a short title area (the app writes Send how? or Receive how?).

assets.name: choose_popup.png
assets.description: The pop-up box with the two big buttons, transparent around it, no title text.

regions.label: title_area
regions.action: the app writes 'Send how?' or 'Receive how?' here

regions.label: same_wifi_button
regions.action: tap to share on the same Wi-Fi or hotspot (the original way)

regions.label: anywhere_button
regions.action: tap to share from anywhere (beta)

pages.name: Anywhere (beta)
pages.purpose: Shown while this phone shares from anywhere. The person sends the other person a link, they open it in any browser, and this phone approves.
pages.notes: Used for both sending and receiving. Paint: the title, three short steps (1 Send them the link. 2 They open it in any browser, nothing to install. 3 You approve when they connect.), the big Share link button with its words, a small sample QR icon labelled Show QR, and the Stop button with its words. The sample QR should look like a QR but must NOT be a real scannable code. The local Same Wi-Fi screens are not changing. Leave the code, status and expiry areas empty: the app writes live text there.

assets.name: anywhere.png
assets.description: The full Anywhere screen as it should look, with the buttons in place and the live-text areas empty.

regions.label: share_button
regions.action: tap to share the link with the phone's share sheet (Messages, WhatsApp, email, copy)

regions.label: qr_button
regions.action: tap to open the QR code overlay. Make the tap area at least 150 px square even if the icon is smaller

regions.label: code_area
regions.action: the app writes the 6-digit code and the website name here, for reading aloud

regions.label: status_line
regions.action: the app writes the latest activity here, for example 'Waiting for the other person'

regions.label: expires_area
regions.action: the app writes 'Link works for 10 minutes' here

regions.label: stop_button
regions.action: tap to stop sharing

pages.name: Anywhere QR overlay
pages.purpose: A pop-up showing the real QR code, for when the other person is nearby or on a video call.
pages.notes: Just the frame on a transparent background; it floats over a dimmed screen. The QR square must be plain white, square and at least 640 px wide (QR codes need the contrast). The app draws the real QR inside it and writes the code text below. Add a close button; tapping anywhere also closes it.

assets.name: anywhere_qr.png
assets.description: The pop-up frame with the plain white QR square, an empty code text area and a close button, transparent around it.

regions.label: qr_square
regions.action: the app draws the real QR code here (keep it plain white, at least 640 px wide)

regions.label: code_area
regions.action: the app writes the 6-digit code and the website name here

regions.label: close_button
regions.action: tap to close the overlay

pages.name: Web page
pages.purpose: The page the OTHER phone sees in its browser, either to download the files being sent or to choose files to upload. One look is shared by both.
pages.notes: This is a web page, not an app screen, so keep the files small (a few hundred KB each at most). The page text, file names, buttons and progress bars are drawn by code, so these files are only the decoration.

assets.name: web_mockup.png
assets.description: A picture of how the page should look, with the header and background. Placeholder text is fine.

assets.name: web_header.png
assets.description: The banner or logo strip across the top of the page.

assets.name: web_background.png
assets.description: The page background. It can be a small tile or a plain gradient.

pages.name: App icon
pages.purpose: The icon on the phone's home screen.
pages.notes: Android crops icons into a circle or rounded square, so keep the important art inside the middle two thirds. Two layers so Android can animate and shape it.

assets.name: icon_foreground.png
assets.description: The icon art on a transparent background, kept inside the middle two thirds.

assets.name: icon_background.png
assets.description: The icon background, edge to edge, no transparency.

assets.name: icon_preview.png
assets.description: What the finished icon looks like.
